## Frontier AI ranking — August 2026

There is **no single definitive “most powerful” model**: rankings change by benchmark, reasoning setting, and whether the task is chat, coding agents, or multimodal work. But the current evidence puts **Anthropic and OpenAI at the overall frontier**, with Google and Grok close behind in particular areas.

| Overall position | Model family / flagship | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **1** | **Claude Opus 5 / Claude Fable 5** | Artificial Analysis gives **Opus 5 (max) 61** on its composite Intelligence Index, narrowly ahead of Fable 5 (60) and GPT‑5.6 Sol (59). Fable 5 leads Arena’s agent benchmark; Opus 5 leads Arena’s text and WebDev rankings. ([artificialanalysis.ai](https://artificialanalysis.ai/articles/opus-5?utm_source=openai)) |
| **2** | **OpenAI GPT‑5.6 Sol** | The strongest GPT variant for difficult reasoning/coding. It is **second on Artificial Analysis’ composite index (59)** and leads its Coding Agent Index (80); OpenAI says Sol is its flagship complex-work model. ([artificialanalysis.ai](https://artificialanalysis.ai/articles/gpt-5-6-has-landed?utm_source=openai)) |
| **3** | **Google Gemini 3.5 / 3.6 Flash** | Google’s newest fast frontier line: Gemini 3.5 Flash is claimed to beat Gemini 3.1 Pro on most benchmarks while running four times faster. Artificial Analysis lists Gemini 3.5 and 3.6 Flash at **50** on its composite index—below the very top Claude/GPT configurations, but highly competitive for speed and cost. ([blog.google](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/technology/developers-tools/google-io-2026-developer-highlights/?utm_source=openai)) |
| **4** | **xAI Grok 4.5** | Grok 4.5 scores **54** on Artificial Analysis’ composite index and is particularly strong for coding agents: it tied GPT‑5.6 Sol on one SWE‑Atlas-QnA evaluation, while Arena places it in the WebDev top 10. ([artificialanalysis.ai](https://artificialanalysis.ai/articles/grok-4-5-brings-spacexai-to-the-the-intelligence-frontier?utm_source=openai)) |

### Best by use case
- **Hardest general reasoning / knowledge work:** **Claude Opus 5** or **Claude Fable 5**. ([artificialanalysis.ai](https://artificialanalysis.ai/articles/opus-5?utm_source=openai))  
- **Coding agents and terminal work:** **GPT‑5.6 Sol**; **Claude Opus 5** is also #1 in Arena’s WebDev human-preference ranking. ([artificialanalysis.ai](https://artificialanalysis.ai/articles/gpt-5-6-has-landed?utm_source=openai))  
- **Fast, lower-cost frontier model:** **Gemini 3.6 Flash** or **GPT‑5.6 Luna**; Gemini is especially positioned around high throughput. ([blog.google](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/technology/developers-tools/google-io-2026-developer-highlights/?utm_source=openai))  
- **Grok:** **Grok 4.5** is frontier-tier, especially for agentic coding, but independent composite rankings currently place it behind the leading Claude and GPT configurations. ([artificialanalysis.ai](https://artificialanalysis.ai/articles/grok-4-5-brings-spacexai-to-the-the-intelligence-frontier?utm_source=openai))  

**Bottom line:** If choosing one “most powerful” model today, pick **Claude Opus 5 / Fable 5** for broad maximum capability; choose **GPT‑5.6 Sol** if elite coding-agent performance and cost-efficiency matter most.

queries.answer:
## Frontier AI snapshot — August 2026

| Lab | Leading model cited | Standout capabilities | Selected reported benchmarks |
|---|---|---|---|
| **OpenAI** | **GPT‑5.6 Sol** | Broad professional reasoning, coding agents, tool use | 52.7% on Agents’ Last Exam; 72.7% DeepSWE v1.1; 88.8% Terminal‑Bench 2.1. ([openai.com](https://openai.com/index/gpt-5-6/?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Anthropic** | **Claude Opus 4.6** | Long-horizon coding, research/search, computer use, very long context | Leads Terminal‑Bench 2.0, Humanity’s Last Exam, BrowseComp, and GDPval‑AA in Anthropic’s comparison; 76% on the 1M-token MRCR v2 retrieval test. ([anthropic.com](https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-opus-4-6?_bhlid=b00b06e9a815a8d2b6c7e8e8db033da20d1c9f25&utm_source=openai)) |
| **Google DeepMind** | **Gemini 3.6 Flash** | Fast multimodal and agentic work; strong long-context retrieval and computer use | 58.7% SWE‑Bench Pro; 78.0% Terminal‑Bench 2.1; 83.0% OSWorld‑Verified; 91.8% on 128K GDM‑MRCR v2. ([deepmind.google](https://deepmind.google/models/gemini/?utm_source=openai)) |
| **xAI** | **Grok 4.5** | Coding, long-running engineering agents, knowledge work | 62.0% DeepSWE 1.0; xAI reports strong performance on SWE‑Marathon, a multi-hour software-engineering evaluation. ([x.ai](https://x.ai/news/grok-4-5?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Meta** | **Llama 4 Maverick** | Open-weight, natively multimodal model for deployable text/image applications | 1M-token context; 80.5% MMLU‑Pro, 69.8% GPQA Diamond, 43.4% LiveCodeBench, and 73.4% MMMU in Meta’s model card. ([github.com](https://github.com/meta-llama/llama-models/blob/main/models/llama4/MODEL_CARD.md?utm_source=openai)) |

**Bottom line:** The frontier has shifted from static chat/reasoning toward **agentic coding, tool and computer use, long-horizon task execution, and usable million-token context**. On overlapping coding-agent tests, no single model dominates universally: OpenAI is particularly strong on Terminal‑Bench/DeepSWE; Anthropic emphasizes long-running coding, search, and knowledge work; Google combines competitive agents with fast multimodality and context; xAI focuses on engineering trajectories; and Meta remains the leading major **open-weight** alternative.

**Important caveat:** these are mostly developer-published figures, often using different versions, scaffolds, tool access, compute budgets, and test subsets. Treat cross-vendor leaderboard claims as directional—not a clean, apples-to-apples ranking.

queries.answer:
## 2026 frontier-model snapshot

There is **no single definitive leaderboard**: results depend on the evaluation harness, prompting, tools/agents, and whether scores are vendor-reported. For the benchmarks you named, the clearest current picture is:

| Capability | Leading model / result | Takeaway |
|---|---:|---|
| **GPQA Diamond** (hard science reasoning) | **Gemini 3.1 Pro — 94.3%** | Best reported score in Crosshair’s current comparison. ([crosshairintelligence.com](https://www.crosshairintelligence.com/models/gemini-3-1-pro)) |
| **SWE-bench Verified** (agentic software engineering) | **Claude Opus 4.8 — 88.6%**; **Claude Opus 4.7 — 87.6%** | Anthropic’s Opus line leads the listed results; these are system/vendor-reported scores, not a pure base-model test. ([crosshairintelligence.com](https://www.crosshairintelligence.com/)) |
| **General coding** | **Qwen3.7 Max — 91.6% LiveCodeBench** | Strongest explicitly reported LiveCodeBench score in the current Crosshair table; DeepSeek V4-Pro follows at 93.5% in that table, which illustrates how score definitions/data may not be consistently presented—treat aggregator rankings cautiously. ([crosshairintelligence.com](https://www.crosshairintelligence.com/)) |
| **Abstract reasoning** | **Gemini 3.1 Pro — 77.1% ARC-AGI-2** | Google reports this as a verified ARC-AGI-2 result; it is a better current reasoning discriminator than saturated classic benchmarks. ([blog.google](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/gemini-models/gemini-3-1-pro/)) |
| **MMLU** (broad academic knowledge) | **Not a useful 2026 differentiator** | MMLU’s commonly indexed leaderboard is stale—e.g., it still shows GPT‑4o at 88.7% from May 2024—while current frontier comparisons tend to use **MMLU-Pro**, GPQA, HLE, and agentic benchmarks instead. ([turingwire.com](https://turingwire.com/benchmarks/)) |

**Practical ranking:**
1. **Best reasoning/science:** Gemini 3.1 Pro  
2. **Best real-world coding agent:** Claude Opus 4.7/4.8  
3. **Best overall choice for difficult coding + reasoning:** Claude Opus for codebase work; Gemini 3.1 Pro for science, multimodal reasoning, and novel logic tasks.  

Use **SWE-bench Verified / Terminal-Bench / LiveCodeBench** for coding-agent selection, and **GPQA Diamond / ARC-AGI-2 / MMLU-Pro** for reasoning selection. SWE-bench itself emphasizes that its leaderboard compares diverse *systems*—from simple model loops to RAG and multi-rollout agents—so scores should not be read as base-model-only capability. ([swebench.com](https://www.swebench.com/verified.html))

content.text:
Big AI model work like this:

1. **Eat lots of words**
   - Model reads huge piles of text, code, images maybe.
   - Books, websites, examples.

2. **Learn patterns**
   - It sees: “sky is ___” often means “blue”.
   - It learns what words usually come next.

3. **Many tiny brain knobs**
   - Model has billions/trillions of “knobs” called parameters.
   - Training turns knobs until answers get better.

4. **You ask question**
   - You type: “explain gravity”.
   - Model breaks your words into small chunks called tokens.

5. **Model predicts next chunk**
   - It guesses one token, then next, then next.
   - Like: “Gravity” → “is” → “a” → “force”...

6. **Looks smart because patterns huge**
   - It learned many patterns: facts, grammar, code, reasoning steps.
   - Not human brain. More like giant pattern machine.

7. **Can be wrong**
   - Sometimes it guesses confidently but wrong.
   - This is called hallucination.

Caveman version:

**AI eat many words. AI learn word patterns. Human ask. AI guess next words very good. Sometimes AI make dumb-dumb.**
